verdict.rationale: Self-hosting applies here because some accelerators are cloud-only, and AMD's docs show the MI355X running on customer-operated infrastructure. Customers can configure, validate and baseline their own Instinct GPUs, deploy them in their own Kubernetes clusters or Docker runtimes, and run the open-source ROCm stack with self-run inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang. missing for 10: dedicated on-prem installation and procurement documentation beyond one-line index summaries, independent or hands-on reports of self-hosted MI355X deployments.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Customer Acceptance Guide Configure, validate, benchmark, and baseline Instinct GPUs.
GPU Operator Deploy and manage Instinct GPUs in Kubernetes clusters.
AMD Container Toolkit Integrate Instinct GPUs with Docker and container runtimes.
Cluster Validation Suite Test scripts that validate AMD AI clusters end to end.
ROCm is AMD’s open-source GPU computing platform: an end‑to‑end ecosystem of compilers, runtimes, and libraries for AI, HPC, and domain‑specific workloads.
